posts.title: Weekly accessible-job digest idea
posts.body: What if Sahaay emailed a weekly digest of new jobs matching our profiles? It would save so much time. Or even better — an in-app notification when a matching job appears!
comments: Great idea, an in-app alert would be perfect.

posts.title: Screen-reader friendly website request
posts.body: Sahaay is great, but I'd love proper ARIA labels on the community cards. Small thing, big difference for low-vision users. Thanks for listening!

posts.title: Support: dealing with workplace anxiety
posts.body: Starting a new job is tough, and with autism the first weeks are overwhelming. Any tips on communicating needs to employers without fear? This community helped me before and I trust it again.
comments: Be clear about what helps you.

posts.title: New hearing-care services at our clinic
posts.body: We've added free monthly hearing screenings at Sunrise Hearing Care. Fully accessible premises, and a sign-language interpreter joins on request. Book through the Healthcare page!
comments: This is really helpful, thank you!

posts.title: Learning ISL — my weekly practice routine
posts.body: I practice the alphabet every morning for 10 minutes, then three word signs. The lessons here with example usage make it so much easier. Anyone want to form a weekly practice group?
comments: Count me in for a practice group.

posts.title: How I found an accessible job through Sahaay
posts.body: After months of searching, I finally found a company that really understood my needs. The accessibility filter and accommodation details made all the difference. Happy to answer questions for anyone looking!

signs.how: Practise forming the letter A with one hand in front of your chest.
Practise forming the letter B with one hand in front of your chest.
Practise forming the letter C with one hand in front of your chest.
Practise forming the letter D with one hand in front of your chest.
Practise forming the letter E with one hand in front of your chest.
Practise the signs for Help, Stop and Call a doctor. Sign them clearly and firmly.
Practise Hello, Good morning, How are you and Thank you in one short conversation.
Hold up 1 finger(s) clearly, palm facing forward.
Hold up 2 finger(s) clearly, palm facing forward.
Hold up 5 finger(s) clearly, palm facing forward.
Point to the person, then raise your eyebrows and open both hands.
Sign "I", then the sign for Help.
Hold both hands up, palms out, and wiggle the fingers.
Make F shapes with both hands and circle them together.
Wave your open hand near your forehead.
Place one fist on the other open palm and lift both up.
Touch fingers to your chin and move the hand forward.
Make a W with three fingers and tap near your chin.
